subject: Request: recovery tolerance and regional redundancy carveout
messages:
From: Jane Miller <jane.miller@oakmontbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@oakmontbank.com
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: recovery tolerance for multi-region failover

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As Oakmont finalizes the controls matrix for our enterprise contract, compliance is asking us to document acceptable recovery tolerances for each geographic footprint and any carveouts when warm-standby cannot be guaranteed. Attached is our standard SLA worksheet (Oakmont_SLA_Request_202605.pdf).

Key asks:
- Can Redwood accept an RTO of 6 hours and RPO of 4 hours for an isolated APAC region when warm-standby is not provisioned?
- How do you handle read-only islanding vs full failover? Are there gradations we can include in the SOW?
- Any evidence you can provide around cross-region restore sequencing and expected data rehydration time?

We want to avoid a blanket exclusion for certain regions if there are programmatic mitigations your team can document. Procurement has been copied; if acceptable, they'll attach this as an addendum to the MSA.

Thanks,
Jane Miller
Director, Cloud Risk & Resilience
Oakmont Bank

Attachment: Oakmont_SLA_Request_202605.pdf (1 page - worksheet)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jane Miller <jane.miller@oakmontbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: recovery tolerance for multi-region failover

Hi Jane — thanks for the worksheet and the clear asks. Copying the folks who will own the SOW language and the technical annex.

Short answers up front:
- We can accept a constrained carveout for APAC with RTO 6h / RPO 4h under a documented conditional activation policy, provided the customer agrees to the standby creation window and capacity reservation terms.
- We support a staged failure mode (read-only islanding followed by progressive rehydration) that reduces immediate customer-impacting writes while recovery completes; this can be described as a mitigation tier in the SOW.
- We will share a cross-region rehydration profile and a sample sequencing playbook; see proposed deliverables below.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
1) Redwood to provide: rehydration sequencing doc, estimated token/GB rehydrate rate by instance class, and an appendix describing conditional activation triggers. (Deliverable: redwood-drafter-sla-v1.xlsx)
2) Oakmont to confirm which regions are subject to the carveout and the acceptable maintenance blackout windows for standby creation.
3) Both sign an SLA addendum that enumerates fallback states (full failover, read-only island, delayed rehydrate) and associated SLOs.

Kimberly, Marissa — can you take point on drafting the SLO table and the customer-facing language for the read-only island approach? Aditya — we may need a short performance estimate for rehydration velocity that we can put in the appendix.

Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: redwood-drafter-sla-v1.xlsx (workbook - draft SLO/scope)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: recovery tolerance for multi-region failover

Thanks — I've started the SLO matrix in the draft spreadsheet. A few notes / suggestions for the addendum language:

- Scope of carveout: limit to regions where customer declines dedicated standby capacity. If Oakmont accepts reserved standby (Committed Dedicated), we will not apply the exception.

- Failover states (examples to include):
  * Tier 1: Active-active (no customer impact) — RTO minutes, RPO seconds.
  * Tier 2: Read-only islanding (ingest paused, read traffic served) — RTO 0-2h for local reads, writes deferred; RPO up to 2h as buffered writes are journaled for later rehydrate.
  * Tier 3: Conditional cold-failover (standby not present) — RTO up to 6h, RPO up to 4h; progressive rehydrate with prioritization for critical prefixes.

- Evidence & testing: propose quarterly DR drills for carveout regions for first 12 months post-go-live, with a runbook artifact and a one-page RTO/RPO evidence summary attached to each drill. This addresses the "evidence" ask.

- Penalties & credits: propose SLA credits only for top-line availability; carveout regions will have a reduced severity table and a cap consistent with our regional liability policy.

Draft language attached in the "SLO_Table" sheet. Marissa — can you convert the matrix into MSA-friendly prose and pull in the liability cap numbers?

Kimberly Park
Head of Reliability Contracts
Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Karthik — appreciate the swift turnaround and the pragmatic approach. Procurement and I had a quick review; Oakmont is amenable to the conditional carveout under the following clarifications: 

1) Carveout limited to APAC & SEA regions only, documented in the annex.
2) Quarterly DR drills required for the first 12 months; evidence to be an ops report signed by Oakmont on completion.
3) RTO/RPO for the carveout tier: RTO <= 6 hours, RPO <= 4 hours. Reedemable credits for availability reductions will be limited to a single-tier lower credit band for carveout events.

Next steps: please send the revised SLO table and a one-page rehydration profile for APAC by EOD Wednesday; procurement will then circulate the addendum for legal redlines and DocuSign. We will attach the finalized addendum to the MSA if the language is accepted.

If you can include the expected data rehydrate throughput per hour (GB/hr) and the prioritized object list (critical prefixes), that would help speed approval.

Thanks,
Jane Miller
Director, Cloud Risk & Resilience
Oakmont Bank

Forwarded attachment request: please include redwood-drafter-sla-v1.xlsx and a brief test plan (DR drill checklist).
